justification: The passage states that wear 'gathers in the length that sweeps the ground and in the two or three links either side of the swivel', which is exactly the two locations B names. A is contradicted by 'a chain condemned for losing a fifth of its diameter is usually condemned on a single bad metre' - the loss is local, not uniform across every link. C (salt corrosion) is never mentioned, and D transfers 'the inshore aids, where the water is narrow' from Cadell's concession about scope onto wear, which the text never says.

Scope buys a circle: 'wind and tide swing the buoy about its sinker, and the more chain it has, the wider the ground it can wander over, so the light is somewhere inside that circle rather than on the cross printed on the chart.' A displaced buoy is therefore normally riding inside its allowed circle rather than having dragged its sinker, which is C. B reverses the stated relation (more chain, not less, widens the wander), A turns the single 31 m / 11 m example into a rule, and D is not addressed.

The lightship paragraph exists to show that positional uncertainty long predates the loggers: her logs carry three bearings watch after watch 'because a moored ship does not sit still either and her keepers knew it', and Fewtrell says 'We knew the shoal was under us... Where we were over it was another question.' That is A. B is the opposite of what the text says, C invents a post-war account of manned stations disappearing, and D draws a comparison with today's crews that the text never makes.

The text says plainly: 'Cadell has read the recordings and concedes the inshore aids, where the water is narrow. On the outer stations he has not moved.' That is D. A overstates the concession into abandonment, B invents a cost argument where his stated reason is that a short-moored buoy 'takes the sea in its chain rather than in the water, and it is the chain that fails', and C invents a chronology the text does not give.

The article follows a tender lifting and relaying buoy 43, explains why a mooring must be slack and what that slack costs in positional accuracy, then sets Cadell against Prigent and closes with 'Neither record disposes of the other.' That is B. A and D take single details (the lightship; crew costs) for the whole, and C makes the piece an argument for loggers, which its even-handed close refuses to be.

A founder 'bills bronze by the kilo and tuning by the hour', and the text gives both ends: 'On a thirty-kilo bell the tuning can come to more than half of what the parish pays; on a bell of a tonne, where the same five partials take not much longer to find, the bronze is the larger part of the bill.' That is exactly D. A ('always') is killed by the tonne case, B by the two separate billing bases, and C by 'take not much longer to find'.

Corvenden 'tunes the hum, the prime and the nominal closely and leaves the minor third near where the casting put it' - three partials tuned close, the minor third left as cast, which is B. A describes Voregg, who brings all of them 'inside four cents of the figures the theory gives'; C is not in the text; D inverts which partial she leaves alone.

Because thinning only lowers a partial and 'Nothing pulls it back up', 'That one-way arrow is why founders cast heavy' - the bell leaves the mould with 'an allowance of metal... that exists only to be turned away'. Tuning all five tightly therefore requires that metal to be there first, which is A. B is contradicted by 'Each partial answers to a band of metal at a particular height inside the bell', C is not addressed, and D's 'always' overstates a claim the text presents as contested.

The writer sets out Voregg's tolerances and Corvenden's objection, reports the one trial that bears on it - 'There is some evidence for her, and Voregg does not pretend there is not' - then gives Voregg's caveat and notes that the decisive experiment 'costs two bells, and no parish has ordered it'. He picks no side, which is C. B fails because the text names an experiment that would settle the question; A overreads a trial the writer explicitly qualifies; D is the reverse of the text.

The piece explains the five partials and how thinning tunes them, prices that work against the bronze, and then shows that 'How far to chase those five is where the trade divides' - that is D. A takes the cost paragraph for the whole and misstates it for heavy bells, B inflates a subordinate remark about tin loss into the subject, and C is not addressed.

The school's row is 'a row of boxes in the same position on the same kind of gable' that 'fills most summers', which is C. A hardens 'most summers' into every summer, B invents fitting dates for both rows that the text never gives, and D is not addressed.

Talbourne's loggers show the animals 'high and deep in the warm hours, when the young grow fastest, out towards the cooler eaves at night', which is D. A reverses that pattern, C is contradicted by 'by dawn the whole void has given its heat back', and B's heat rising from the rooms below is never mentioned.

'Both of those two sat on a chimney breast whose flue still carried warm air up from the block's boiler, and the loggers inside them recorded a swing much like the timber's' - the range came from the flue behind, not from the box, which is A. B is contradicted by 'cast boxes on two other south-facing walls, with nothing behind them but insulation, stayed empty', and those same empty boxes also sink C. D is not in the text.

The writer grants the timing objection exactly as far as the early record goes - 'On the early boxes she was plainly right, and Talbourne says so' - and then reports the second series, which held timing constant ('all fitted out of season') and still split timber from cast. That is C. A is contradicted by that second series, D by the writer's explicit agreement with her, and B invents a complaint about the size of her file search.

The piece opens on eleven years of empty boxes at the laundry against a row that 'fills most summers' four streets away, and spends the rest weighing thermal range against fitting season as the explanation - that is B. A and D mistake the planning and council framing for the subject, and C misreads three summers of logging temperatures as giving up counting altogether.

The passage states the loan and repayment were both in grain: “Den som fick en tunna råg i mars skulle vid skörden lämna tillbaka lika mycket, jämte ett tillägg — vanligen en åttondel — också det i råg.” A is contradicted by “Ingen sedel behövde växlas” and by the same sentence (repayment in rye, not money). B invents an annually set surcharge, whereas the text fixes it at “vanligen en åttondel”. D is directly contradicted: “Vad magasinet däremot inte kunde göra var att sprida risken.”

The 1798 ordinance is quoted as “Den som inte hade betalat tillbaka till Mikaeli, i slutet av september, fick stå över utlåningen följande vår”, which is exactly A. B is contradicted by “Magasinet fick öppnas endast när två personer var på plats, och de båda låsen hade skilda nycklar”, with the second key held by the föreståndare. C is contradicted by “Varje utlåning skulle skrivas in samma dag.” D is contradicted because the föreståndare was the one “som sockenstämman valt”, not appointed by the priest.

The stated objection is that the book's own appendix undercuts the savings-bank explanation: “I den förteckning över avvecklade magasin som avslutar boken ligger de tidigaste nedläggningarna i Hässle härad flera decennier före den första sparbanken i samma härad.” A is false because the reviewer credits Grimlund with raising the 1863 reform (“Han antyder själv två”, including “kommunreformen 1863”). B misapplies the Bjärnhult protocol, which the reviewer praises and which concerns bookkeeping, not the wind-down. C overstates: “nedläggningen i tre av de socknar han följer sammanfaller väl med sparbankens tillkomst”.

The reviewer explicitly rejects the idea that these buildings are a digression: “Grimlund noterar sådant i förbigående, som om det vore en avvikelse från ämnet. Det är det inte. Att en socken kunde göra sig av med inrättningen men behålla huset säger något om vad man ansåg vara värt att spara.” That is B: the houses carry more about the parish's values than Grimlund realises. A is contradicted by that same passage; C reverses it (Grimlund passes over the houses rather than dwelling on them); D's fieldwork-versus-archives contrast is never addressed — the notes point “genomgående till arkiv”.

The text says outright: "Wear is not spread evenly along the chain either. It gathers in the length that sweeps the ground and in the two or three links either side of the swivel." B restates both sites. A is contradicted by "a chain condemned for losing a fifth of its diameter is usually condemned on a single bad metre"; salt corrosion (C) is never mentioned, and the inshore/narrow-water remark belongs to Cadell's concession, not to wear (D).

The mechanism is stated: "wind and tide swing the buoy about its sinker, and the more chain it has, the wider the ground it can wander over, so the light is somewhere inside that circle rather than on the cross printed on the chart." C is that implication exactly, and Prigent's loggers confirm it — "the buoys laid longest sit as much as 35 metres from their charted places for hours together." B reverses the relation (more chain, not less, means a wider circle); A promotes one boat's "thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water" into a rule; an early lift (D) is never suggested.

The lightship's logs "carry, watch after watch, three bearings taken on the shore marks, because a moored ship does not sit still either and her keepers knew it," and Fewtrell says: "We knew the shoal was under us... Where we were over it was another question." That is positional uncertainty recorded long before Prigent began "fitting position loggers inside the hulls since 2019," which is A. B is contradicted by "does not sit still either"; C over-reads a single withdrawal made when "the harbour board set the cost of her crew against a lamp on a hull that needed none"; D compares old and present crews, which the text never does.

"Cadell has read the recordings and concedes the inshore aids, where the water is narrow. On the outer stations he has not moved." That is D verbatim in substance. A is contradicted by the same sentence; his defence is survival, not relative cost — "A buoy that rides easy, he argues, comes through a February gale and a winter of drift ice" (B); and nothing links his practice to the storm that cost the district two aids (C).

The piece follows a lift — "buoy 43 comes up out of the Cleyburn approaches" — explains scope and its cost ("What scope costs is a circle"), and then sets Cadell against Prigent on how much slack to give, closing "Neither record disposes of the other." That is B. The lightship (A) is one supporting section; loggers-for-all (C) is Prigent's wish, not the article's thesis; and cost of crewless maintenance (D) appears only in the 1968 withdrawal.

"On a thirty-kilo bell the tuning can come to more than half of what the parish pays; on a bell of a tonne, where the same five partials take not much longer to find, the bronze is the larger part of the bill" — precisely D. A's "always" is contradicted by the tonne case; B is contradicted by "a founder bills bronze by the kilo and tuning by the hour"; C is contradicted by "Lathe time... does not scale the way metal does."

"She tunes the hum, the prime and the nominal closely and leaves the minor third near where the casting put it" — three partials close, the minor third as cast, which is B. A describes Voregg, who "brings all of them inside four cents of the figures the theory gives, and can name the tolerance on any bell"; C and D invert or invent her method — she works on the lathe like Kerrig, and the hum is one of the three she tunes closely.

Tuning is subtractive and irreversible — "thinning that band pulls the partial down. Nothing pulls it back up" — and "That one-way arrow is why founders cast heavy. A bell leaves the mould thicker and sharper than the drawing asks for, carrying an allowance of metal... that exists only to be turned away." So chasing all five tightly requires more metal in the mould first: A. B is contradicted by "Each partial answers to a band of metal at a particular height inside the bell"; fittings and frames (C) are never discussed; D's "always" overstates Corvenden's contested claim.

The writer lays out Voregg's tolerance practice and Corvenden's objection, concedes "There is some evidence for her, and Voregg does not pretend there is not," reports the Ockthorne trial and Voregg's own limit on it — "One afternoon, one tower, bells of different weights... I would not build a workshop on that. I would not throw it away either" — and closes without adjudicating. That is C. B is wrong because the text names "the experiment that would settle the question"; A and D each attribute a verdict the writer withholds.

The article explains the partials ("A bell is not one note but a stack of them... the hum... the prime... a minor third, a fifth, and the nominal"), what the work costs ("a founder bills bronze by the kilo and tuning by the hour"), and the dispute over how far to take it ("How far to chase those five is where the trade divides") — all three strands, which only D covers. A takes the cost strand alone; B misstates the recovery remark ("a foundry that keeps its bins swept recovers most of what the lathe takes off"); C names topics the text does not treat.

"Four streets away, on a school converted the same year, a row of boxes in the same position on the same kind of gable fills most summers" — used in most summers, same position as the laundry's, which is C. A hardens "most summers" into every one; the school row's fitting season is never given (B); and the three summers of logging were Talbourne's temperature work, not a survey of that row before the planning condition (D).

"Talbourne's loggers show the animals working through that gradient: high and deep in the warm hours, when the young grow fastest, out towards the cooler eaves at night" — warm end by day, cool end after dark: D. A reverses it; C is contradicted by "by dawn the whole void has given its heat back"; the heat source is the roof, "Slate heats quickly," not the rooms below (B).

"Both of those two sat on a chimney breast whose flue still carried warm air up from the block's boiler, and the loggers inside them recorded a swing much like the timber's" — the range came from behind the box, not from the casting, which is A. B is contradicted by "cast boxes on two other south-facing walls, with nothing behind them but insulation, stayed empty"; those empty walls also refute C; no difference in the mix is ever mentioned (D).

The writer grants her the first record — "On the early boxes she was plainly right, and Talbourne says so" — but then reports the controlled series, "all fitted out of season and all logged," in which nine of twelve timber boxes filled and only two cast ones did, both on a warm flue. Acceptance as far as the early boxes, not beyond: C. A would make material irrelevant, which the second series denies; the writer never questions her file work as too small (B) or treats it as already answered (D).

The article opens on boxes that have "never held a bat" beside a row that "fills most summers" and spends the rest on the competing explanations — thermal range versus fitting season — for that difference. That is B. Planning conditions (A) are the framing device; Talbourne logged temperatures "rather than counting animals" for three summers but that is a method note, not the subject (C); and D misdescribes the officers' disagreement, which is about roosts, not about how much fabric to retain.

The passage describes the loan and its repayment as being in the same commodity: “Den som fick en tunna råg i mars skulle vid skörden lämna tillbaka lika mycket, jämte ett tillägg — vanligen en åttondel — också det i råg.” That is C word for word. A is contradicted by “Ingen sedel behövde växlas.”, B invents an annually negotiated supplement where the text fixes it at “vanligen en åttondel”, and D is contradicted by “Vad magasinet däremot inte kunde göra var att sprida risken.”

The 1798 ordinance is quoted as barring a defaulter from the next lending round: “Den som inte hade betalat tillbaka till Mikaeli, i slutet av september, fick stå över utlåningen följande vår.” That is exactly A. B is contradicted by “de båda låsen hade skilda nycklar: kyrkvärden bar den ena, den föreståndare som sockenstämman valt bar den andra” together with “Magasinet fick öppnas endast när två personer var på plats”; C is contradicted by “Varje utlåning skulle skrivas in samma dag.”; D is contradicted because the föreståndare was elected by the sockenstämma, not appointed by the priest.

The reviewer's objection is that Grimlund's savings-bank explanation is undercut by his own appendix: “I den förteckning över avvecklade magasin som avslutar boken ligger de tidigaste nedläggningarna i Hässle härad flera decennier före den första sparbanken i samma härad.” That is D. A is contradicted because he does raise the reform — “Och kommunreformen 1863 lämnade oklart vem som egentligen ägde magasinet” — the complaint being only that it stands “i förbigående”; C overstates the case against “nedläggningen i tre av de socknar han följer sammanfaller väl med sparbankens tillkomst”; B misassigns the Bjärnhult protocol, which the reviewer cites approvingly and about the gap between rule and practice, not about the winding-up.

The reviewer raises the re-used buildings precisely to overrule Grimlund's own estimate of them: “Grimlund noterar sådant i förbigående, som om det vore en avvikelse från ämnet. Det är det inte.”, adding that keeping the house “säger något om vad man ansåg vara värt att spara”. That is B. A is contradicted by “Det är det inte.”, C reverses the text (it is Grimlund who passes over the buildings, not dwells on them), and D is not addressed anywhere — the notes point to archives, not fieldwork.

findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE lean to B ("It builds up where the chain drags on the bottom and close to the swivel"): marine-engineering knowledge that mooring-chain wear concentrates at the seabed touchdown/sweep zone and at the swivel. No structural tell — A (quantified per-link loss), C (corrosion outweighs abrasion) and D (inshore aids worst) are all substantively plausible passage claims, and a reader without marine knowledge sees four parallel options. Passage still needed to decide; routed to adjudication, not killed.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE pick C ("It may be riding the edge of the circle its chain allows, not dragging its sinker"): the watch-circle account is the standard physical explanation for an off-charted buoy, and the same physics inverts B ("The less chain it has been given, the further from its charted cross it is likely to lie") — more scope, not less, widens the circle. Mechanism is domain knowledge, so flag not kill; B is a well-aimed misconception distractor.

Mild test-wiseness tell: C is the only option that concedes and rejects an alternative ("may be ... not ..."), while A asserts "must" and D asserts "will". The hedge asymmetry is only 2-2 (B also hedges with "likely"), so this is a soft attractor, not a lethal hedged-among-absolutes leak.

PARTIALLY answerable by form: B ("the manned vessel held its station more faithfully than the buoy does") and D ("the old keepers may have watched their position more closely than today's crews") are a near-duplicate pair — both assert the manned arrangement was better on position — and a test-wise reader discards mutually-undermining near-duplicates with no domain knowledge at all.

C ("To account for the disappearance of manned stations from the coast after the war") is off the unit's scope: no other stem or option in the sheet touches the decline of manned stations, so it reads as filler from the sheet alone. Eliminations leave A, but D's hedge ("may have") keeps it live, so the item is not decided blind — flag rather than kill.

Cross-question channel with q:5. q:5 option B names "an unsettled argument about slack", and q:4's own stem ("Cadell's practice of laying his buoys long") plus options naming Prigent's loggers identify that argument. If the argument is unsettled, A ("He has given it up since reading what Prigent's loggers recorded") is disfavoured because it settles it. The channel runs both ways: q:4 supplies the dispute that makes q:5/B recognisable, and q:5/B trims q:4's option set.

Weak nuance attractor: D is the only two-part partial-concession option ("conceded the inshore aids ... but not the outer stations"), the shape test-wise readers favour. Confidence is low — B (cost defence) and C (storm origin) remain substantively live passage claims, so the item is not decided blind.

Strongest within-unit channel in the sheet: B ("What keeping a floating light on station involves, and an unsettled argument about slack") is reconstructible from the sibling stems alone — q:1 chain wear, q:2 a buoy off its charted position, q:3 a marked position before loggers, q:4 "Cadell's practice of laying his buoys long" (i.e. slack). Both halves of B are spelled out by the other four questions without the passage and without domain knowledge.

Breadth tell within q:5 alone: B is the only balanced two-part descriptive option, while A is narrow-scope history, C is advocacy ("ought to be fitted"), and D is a cost thesis. A main-idea key being the broadest option is the ordinary shape of authentic HP main-idea items, so per the gate's calibration this is flagged for adjudication rather than killed.

findings.quote: Tuning can cost more than the bronze on a small bell, and less than it on a heavy one.
findings.note: Labour-vs-metal economics (metal cost scales with mass, lathe labour far less so) makes D the true real-world statement, and it is also the only two-sided conditional among three flat generalisations ('always takes a larger share', 'a single price for each kilo', 'far longer to tune'). The distractors are substantive trade claims a passage would have to decide, so this is world-knowledge answerability, not a form-only leak.

findings.quote: The bell has to leave the mould heavier, since the metal tuning removes must be there first.
findings.note: Standard founding practice - bells are cast with a tuning allowance because lathe tuning only removes metal - decides A on domain knowledge, and A's own justifying clause is close to self-evident. B, C and D are substantive claims a passage would still have to ground, so flag rather than a structural leak.

findings.quote: He treats the disagreement as a matter of taste that measurement can never settle.
findings.note: Two options fall passage-blind: B is undercut because A and C both presuppose an actual trial exists, and D's 'workshop folklore that the measurements have already disposed of' is the overreaching dismissal typical of filler. A (mild lean) versus C (even-handed) stays undecided without the text; lean C on expository-genre convention.

findings.quote: How a bell's partials are tuned, what that work costs, and how far founders take it.
findings.note: Main-idea item in which D is the compound scope statement that largely subsumes A's cost angle, while B ('recover less of the bronze ... than they generally suppose') is too narrow to be a thesis and C lists a different text's subject. Breadth-wins is a form-level tell, but A remains a live competitor if the text really is price-focused, so partial rather than decided.

findings.quote: The animals were up at the warm end while the afternoon heat lasted, and out at the cool end after dark.
findings.note: Passage-blind I can discount C (a gradient staying as wide at dawn as in the late afternoon is thermally implausible for a void that cools overnight) and lean away from A (day-roosting bats normally hold the warm end while the sun is on the roof), which concentrates the mass on B and D; D is my lean. B - heat rising from the rooms below - stays a substantive and generally true alternative, so the passage is still needed to decide. This is domain reasoning, not a form tell.

findings.quote: Cast boxes work as well as timber ones provided they are hung high on a sunny wall.
findings.note: C is eliminable on scope alone - the stem asks what is suggested about two specific occupied boxes while C answers about cast boxes in general - and D is counter-directional (aggregate that 'gave up its heat more quickly' would argue against occupancy, not for it), leaving A against B. A is my lean, but B (the only cast boxes on a south-facing wall) is an equally substantive competing explanation of the same anomaly, so the item is not decided blind.

findings.quote: Convinced: the writer agrees with her that what a box is made of hardly matters at all.
findings.note: The two extreme stances are discountable blind - A because the sheet's own interest in cast versus timber boxes makes wholesale agreement that material 'hardly matters at all' unlikely, D less firmly - leaving the two qualified stances B and C at roughly even odds. Oyelaran's objection is never stated in the stems, so nothing decides between them: better than chance, not answerable.

findings.quote: Why some purpose-built replacement roosts are taken up by bats while others stand empty.
findings.note: Standard main-idea item: C overstates ('give up counting animals altogether'), while A and D name real but subordinate threads (planning conditions, a disagreement), and the sibling stems - boxes on a converted school, roof voids, occupied cast boxes, temperature - make B the topical fit. The blind answerability comes from the sibling stems and ordinary main-idea option shapes rather than from any tell inside this item, so flag rather than kill.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE pick B ("Luft tränger in, veden brinner upp i stället för att förkolna, och kolningen går förlorad"): this is the canonical fact about a charcoal kiln — air ingress makes the wood combust to ash instead of charring. The same knowledge rules out A and C, which both assert a slower or prolonged outcome. Process comprehension, not a date/name lookup, and a passage would ground it — flag, not RECALL_ONLY.

D ("Varje sådan glipa förstör ofelbart hela lasten, oavsett hur snabbt kolaren hinner ingripa") is eliminable by pure form: an unhedged absolute ("ofelbart", "oavsett") that contradicts the stem's own presupposition, since "om ... inte upptäcks i tid" implies that timely intervention does change the outcome. Stem-entailed elimination, no domain knowledge required.

A is eliminable by pure form: it reverses the stem's premise. The stem presupposes that tar burning could be carried on FURTHER from the buyer than charcoal burning; A makes tar the constrained craft ("fick den bara framställas nära vattenvägar") and charcoal the transport-tolerant one. Logical mismatch with the stem, no domain knowledge needed.

B (bulk plus high value per barrel) and D (charcoal crumbling at transloading, tar tolerating long transport) are BOTH independently true of Swedish bruk economics and both answer the stem directly, so the blind pick splits between them rather than leaking — B taken only on the thin ground that value-density is the fuller transport-economics account. Routed to adjudication as a key-defensibility question for the content gates. C eliminated on domain grounds (resinous pine was not confined to areas remote from the hyttor).

Test-wiseness stack lands on A without the passage: C is over-absolute ("aldrig kan säga något säkert"), D is off-scope (a nitpick about the föreståndare writing only surnames in the 1870s, unrelated to the boundary's interpretation), and B is self-defeating as an "invändning" — saying the works bought forest exactly as far out as the sledges reached identifies the boundary with sledge range, which is the reading it purports to attack. A is the only well-formed alternative-explanation objection and the only hedged one ("kan visa ... inte").

Repair side-effect. The rewritten D carries no transport-economics content, so the q:3 -> q:2 channel is closed (verified from the sheet alone). But D now reads as filler that a blind solver discards on sight, which strengthens the form-based elimination on this question. Not killed: one alternative-explanation option among an absolutist, an off-detail and a muddled option is also the ordinary shape of authentic HP objection items, so per calibration this goes to adjudication.

Two options fall to form. B ("så gott som varje torparhushåll i häradet") is an unwarranted generalisation: the stem says the same household COULD carry on both crafts, B leaps to nearly all households DOING both. D ("tvingades till tjärbränning sedan bruket börjat ta ut allt högre avgifter för lånade kärl") is a causal origin claim that does not answer "vad kan man dra för slutsats av att samma hushåll kunde bedriva båda hantverken" — a stem-form mismatch.

Cross-question cue plus domain knowledge picks C. q:3's options — both A and B — establish winter sledge haulage of charcoal, a seasonal cue in the sheet that corroborates C's "arbetstopparna låg i olika delar av året"; the complementary-season account is also the standard historiography of by-employment. A (shared know-how) stays substantively live, so the item is not decided blind.

Repair side-effect / channel check: the rewritten D contains no bulk, value-per-barrel, friability or transport content, so it does not hand q:2's answer — the q:4 -> q:2 channel is closed, verified from the sheet alone. The cost is that D no longer answers the stem's inferential form, making it a fourth-option discard.

findings.quote: Låntagaren fick säd och lämnade tillbaka lika mycket vid skörden, jämte ett tillägg på vanligen en åttondel.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick C). Domain knowledge of Swedish sockenmagasin decides it: grain was lent in spring and repaid in kind after harvest with interest in natura, commonly one eighth. No form-only asymmetry - A (repayment in money), B (surcharge set annually by the sockenstämma) and D (collective lending at crop failure) are parallel in length and register and are all substantively possible arrangements a passage would have to settle.

findings.quote: Kyrkvärden förvarade båda nycklarna och kunde därför öppna magasinet utan att någon annan var närvarande.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (blind pick A). Knowledge of magasinsordningar - two locks with keys held by different men, entry in the ledger at the moment of lending, shared accountability for the accounts - makes B, C and D read as control failures no ordinance would prescribe, leaving A. A near-structural pattern supports it (three options close on a slackened-control clause: 'utan att någon annan var närvarande', 'behövde inte ... förrän', 'svarade ensam', while A states a sanction), but seeing that pattern as decisive requires assuming the ordinance's purpose was tight control, which is domain inference rather than pure form - hence major, not lethal.

findings.quote: Att han överdriver sparbankernas roll så till den grad att ingen enda av socknarna i boken stöder sambandet.
findings.note: PARTIALLY (blind pick D). No world knowledge is available - Grimlund and the district are invented - so the lean is formal: C is the only option carrying an absolute ('ingen enda') and is a same-topic overstated twin of D, and in such a pair the measured member is the conventional key; D is also the only option whose subject is the explanation itself ('Att den vilar på sparbankerna') rather than the author ('Att han ...'), matching the stem's focus on 'Grimlunds förklaring'. A (the 1863 kommunreform omission) and B (a single stämmoprotokoll carrying the argument) stay substantively open, so the item is materially better than chance blind but not decided.

findings.quote: De hade ett givet mått i fyrkant, medan tjockleken blev den som vinterns kyla råkade ge.
findings.note: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, blind pick C: lake-ice thickness is set by the winter, so harvested blocks are cut to a standard plan measure with the thickness left to the season. A is the physical inverse of that and B is close to self-refuting ('vägde alltid omkring hundrafemtio kilo, oavsett hur kall vintern hade varit'). D remains a substantive detail a passage could carry, so flag.

findings.quote: Att han förbigår kommunreformen 1863, trots att den gjorde det oklart vem som ägde magasinen.
findings.note: ARGUABLE: the substance of this criticism is genuinely in the passage — the reviewer does fault Grimlund for underplaying the alternative explanations ('Men detta står i förbigående, på en dryg sida, och läsaren får själv väga ihop det', 'det hade varit klädsamt att säga det rakt ut') — and the option's second clause is verbatim supported ('kommunreformen 1863 lämnade oklart vem som egentligen ägde magasinet, socknen eller den nya kommunen'). The lure is lexical: 'förbigår' sits one clitic away from 'i förbigående', a phrase the passage uses twice for Grimlund treating something lightly. The case is beatable and no complaint would survive: 'förbigår' asserts omission, and the passage says he raises it himself — 'Han antyder själv två. ... Och kommunreformen 1863 lämnade oklart ...'. The prompt delimiter 'mot Grimlunds förklaring till att magasinen försvann' also points at the explanation he actually advances, which is what the key restates ('bokens eget bilagematerial talar delvis emot honom ... de tidigaste nedläggningarna i Hässle härad flera decennier före den första sparbanken i samma härad'). Flagged, not killed — the key remains clearly best.

comparative_note: Sits comfortably inside the exemplar range. Like host-2021-verb2-ELF-040 (National Geographic History) it reads as a credited magazine excerpt at 4136 characters with five questions - the shape of all 38 authentic long ELF passages - and does the same work of explaining a technical system (scope, wear, the swivel) before opening a genuine unresolved dispute about it, closing on refused resolution the way host-2021 leaves the Pantheon's symbolism contested and var-2022-1-verb1-ELF-031 leaves the grant-cycle constraint on aging research standing. Its scene-led reported voice is more literary than the Pantheon's plain exposition but well inside the attested ELF source range (New Statesman, Guardian Weekly, Time, New African), and it carries exemplar-grade concrete residue - the fog bell, the twice-yearly painting at moorings, the logs 'mostly weather', 214 aids on a three-year cycle, the forty-minute lift - roughly half of which no question touches, which is the opposite of test-manufactured tidiness; the repaired spans 'spring tides' and 'ground swell' are both correct trade usage and read as the crews' own vocabulary. Stems are attested HP families ('What does the text say about ...' and 'What is this text mainly about?' occur verbatim in the authentic ELF corpus; the mention-function stem matches 'Why is Leo Tolstoy mentioned?'), with options in paraphrase register rather than passage lifts; the author-only byline diverges from the corpus 'Author, Publication' line (38/38) but that is the pipeline's mandated publication-neutral anti-plagiarism convention (GENERATION.md section 6), a family-wide house rule rather than a property of this unit, so it is not recorded as a finding.

findings.quote: Time on the lathe rises with a bell's weight, so a bell of a tonne takes far longer to tune.
findings.note: Question style: option rhythm is uniformly long. All 20 options run 14-20 words (median 17) against an authentic ELF median of 10; none is under the corpus p90 of 14. host-2021-verb2-ELF-040's set spans 7-14 words and varies ('The human world versus the world above.' next to a 14-word option). Nothing here exceeds the authentic ELF maximum of 29 words, so this is rhythm, not range.

comparative_note: The restored passage sits comfortably inside the Pantheon exemplar's register: a bylined magazine feature ('Callum Illingsby') dense with unforced particulars (240 kg cast for Larrowden, a 12 kg turning allowance against 228 kg finished, four cents, the 2019 Ockthorne trial where six of the first seven places went to Vennerby and the most precisely tuned bell came ninth) built around a trade disagreement the writer explicitly declines to settle - the same stance as host-2021-verb2-ELF-040's 'much debate over the Pantheon's symbolism' and its 'Even if... do seem to suggest' close. Concrete residue a test-writer would not invent is present throughout, ending on the bin of turnings standing about a third full; there is no reader address, no one-claim-per-paragraph tidiness, and the digression about the experiment that costs two bells is exactly the kind of unresolved aside authentic prose carries. Prompts match the ELF family closely - 'What is implied about...', 'What is the writer's attitude towards...', 'What is this text mainly about?' against the exemplars' 'What is implied in the first two paragraphs?' and 'What is the main point in this text?' - and no option lifts a passage string (longest verbatim run 2 words, against an authentic ELF p99 of 3). Only the uniformly long option rhythm separates it from the exemplars, and it stays inside the authentic band.

findings.quote: Att de båda hantverken byggde på samma kunnande, så att den som behärskade det ena snabbt lärde sig det andra.
findings.note: Question style: three of sixteen options (q1C 19w, q2B 19w, q4A 20w) sit above the authentic LÄS p99 of 18 words, where var-2015-verb2-LÄS-016 and host-2020-verb2-LÄS-020 run 6-12. None exceeds the authentic maximum of 21 words and none uses compound punctuation, so this is at the edge of the range rather than outside it.

comparative_note: Reads as Swedish popular-history prose of the kind LÄS draws on, and is if anything less schematic than var-2019-verb1-LÄS-018, whose exemplar text announces 'problemet är synligt pa tva omraden' and then marches through 'For det forsta' / 'For det andra'. The candidate carries a real, unresolved scholarly dispute - Bostrand's transport-boundary reading, Nyfeldt's ownership-boundary objection, his partial concession in Sladbo and Brantemala, the Strakasen crown-forest counter-case, and her rejoinder that Strakasen is a single area - which is the same 'author declines to close the argument' temperature as host-2020-verb2-LÄS-020. Concrete residue is dense and often argues for nothing at all: the kolardotter who could hear a failing mila before she was ten, the sockenstamma complaints of the 1840s, and above all the Brantemala collier debited in 1868 for fourteen stig that never seem to have been loaded, a debt standing unchanged for twelve years and explicitly unexplained. Options are in paraphrase register throughout (longest verbatim run 4 words, at the authentic LÄS p99); only their length sits at the edge.

findings.quote: Att han låter ett enda stämmoprotokoll bära hela resonemanget om avvecklingen.
findings.note: Question style: this 11-word option is the SHORTEST in the whole unit, so the unit's per-question mean option length never falls below 13.25 words. Across all 94 authentic LÄS passages carrying 4+ questions the highest such floor is 11.8 words (median 5.6), so no authentic set is uniformly long the way this one is; the recension twin var-2013-verb1-LÄS-017..020 puts one-word options (Avlastande / Splittrande) beside a 16-word option in the same set. Recorded as minor, not major: this floor is a batch-wide generator house style (sibling floors 15.5 and 16.5) rather than a defect of this unit, and on every sub-metric las-b14-002 is now the most authentic-like LÄS unit in batch14.

comparative_note: The passage sits comfortably inside the exemplar range and is if anything richer in concrete residue than var-2019-verb1-LÄS-018: the review keeps a real historiographical tension open (Grimlund's sparbank explanation is contradicted by his own appendix, then partly conceded, then explicitly left undecidable) rather than resolving to a settled school-essay claim, which is the same move host-2020-verb2-LÄS-020 makes with its Norway comparison. findings.quote: Tjäran låg still i sina tunnor
findings.note: class 5/6: bare predicative 'still' is the spoken/colloquial variant (as in 'ligg still!'); edited sakprosa uses the invariable standard form 'stilla', and the repo's 2.7 MB authentic-HP corpus shows only 'stilla' in this use (every bare 'still' hit there is English ELF text). In an otherwise high-register essay ('tålde världen olika väl', 'i skarpa ordalag') it reads as a register/form slip. Native alternative: 'Tjäran låg stilla i sina tunnor'.

findings.quote: jämte ett tillägg — vanligen en åttondel — också det i råg
findings.note: class 2 (English punctuation habit): the text uses the English em dash U+2014 as tankstreck throughout (5 occurrences incl. the byline) and no en dash at all; Swedish edited sakprosa sets tankstreck as a spaced en dash. The repo's own authentic HP corpus shows 5139 en dashes against 6 em dashes. Native alternative: 'jämte ett tillägg – vanligen en åttondel – också det i råg'.

findings.quote: de partier som inte tjänar något argument alls
findings.note: class 6 (idiomatic temperature): Swedish 'tjäna' collocates with syfte/sak/tes, so 'tjänar något argument' reads as the English 'serve an argument' stretched onto the Swedish frame. Native alternative: 'de partier som inte tjänar något syfte alls'.

findings.quote: de partier som inte tjänar något argument alls
findings.note: class 6: idiomatic temperature. Swedish 'tjäna' takes abstract objects productively ('tjäna ett syfte', 'tjäna en sak'), but 'tjäna ett argument' is a thin collocation that maps one-to-one onto English 'serve an argument'; a copy editor may pause on it. Native alternative: 'de partier som inte tjänar något syfte alls' or 'de partier som inte driver någon tes'.

findings.quote: as much as 35 metres from their charted places
findings.note: class 4: numeral style breaks the passage's own established convention — every other measurement and count is spelled out ("thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water", "two hundred and fourteen floating aids", "eleven fresh links", "forty minutes"), so a copy editor would normalise this one figure; editor's rewrite: 'as much as thirty-five metres from their charted places'.

findings.quote: It is heaviest on the aids moored inshore, where the channel water is narrow.
findings.note: class 3: "the channel water is narrow" is not an English collocation — the passage's own "where the water is narrow" works because "narrow water(s)" is fixed trade idiom, but premodifying it with "channel" makes a compound noun of which "narrow" cannot naturally be predicated; editor's rewrite: 'where the channel is narrow'.

findings.quote: most of the boxes that failed had been opened in June or July
findings.note: class 3 (idiom/collocation): a bat box is fitted, hung or put up, not 'opened' - the verb belongs to buildings and services, not to a wall-mounted box. The passage itself uses the right verb two sentences later ('those fitted between September and February') and elsewhere ('all fitted out of season', 'You can hang the finest box in the county'), so the slip is visible on the page. editor's rewrite: 'most of the boxes that failed had been fitted in June or July'.

findings.quote: the space near the ridge can stand close to thirty degrees
findings.note: class 2 (preposition choice): a reading stands AT a figure; with the preposition dropped the space appears to 'stand' a temperature rather than register one. editor's rewrite: 'the space near the ridge can stand at close to thirty degrees'.

findings.quote: a lift, a scrape, a fresh lamp and a relay take about forty minutes
findings.note: class 3: 'a relay' garden-paths the reader into the electrical/handover sense; the meaning is 'laying the buoy again', which British house style hyphenates precisely to avoid this collision. Editor's rewrite: 'a lift, a scrape, a fresh lamp and a re-lay take about forty minutes'.

Editor's rewrite: 'where the channel is narrow'.

findings.quote: the buoys laid longest sit as much as 35 metres from their charted places
findings.note: class 4: sole numeral among roughly twenty spelled-out quantities ('thirty-one metres', 'eleven metres', 'two hundred and fourteen', 'forty minutes', 'eleven fresh links'), so the piece's number style is internally inconsistent at one point. Defensible as an instrument-reading contrast, but a copy desk would query. Editor's rewrite: 'as much as thirty-five metres'.

findings.quote: and less than it on a heavy one
findings.note: class 3: grammatical comparative ellipsis, but the pronoun 'it' sits next to 'a small bell' and only resolves to 'the bronze' on a second pass — a copy editor would bracket it and query the referent, and in option text (which must be unambiguous at speed for a Swedish examinee) would spell it out. Editor's rewrite: 'and less than the bronze on a heavy one'. No other conviction: the passage is native-quality British magazine prose — no article errors, no false friends, no Swedish interference, consistent British orthography ('mould', 'neighbours', 'tonne'), consistent no-Oxford-comma house style, and genuinely native idiom ('came ninth', 'the better part of a day', 'forty-odd', 'keeps its bins swept'). Register holds one serious-magazine voice throughout with no AI boilerplate, and texture is concrete (named founders, dated 2019 Ockthorne trial, reconciling weights 240/12/228, hedged claims, dry wit).

findings.quote: most of the boxes that failed had been opened in June or July

findings.quote: the space near the ridge can stand close to thirty degrees
findings.note: class 3: 'stand' before a figure normally takes 'at' ('the temperature stood at thirty degrees'), and with 'the space' as subject against the parallel clause's 'sits ten or twelve degrees below it' the bare 'stand close to' reads clipped. Editor's rewrite: 'the space near the ridge can sit at close to thirty degrees'.

findings.quote: The chain comes up after it, thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water
findings.note: class 2 (grammar -- pronoun reference): 'it' changes referent inside seven words. The first 'it' is buoy 43 (the chain comes up after the buoy, which landed on the afterdeck in the previous sentence); the second 'it' is the chain, so 'thirty-one metres of it' momentarily offers thirty-one metres of buoy. The absurdity of that reading makes it self-correcting, which is why it stays minor rather than major, but it is exactly the kind of second pronoun a copy editor deletes. No Swedish tell -- this is a native compression that a native sub would still tighten. Editor's rewrite: 'The chain comes up after it, thirty-one metres of chain for eleven metres of water, each link a hand's width across and slick.'

findings.quote: small craft now steer to a plotted mark on the assumption that they do not
findings.note: class 2 (grammar -- pronoun reference / stranded ellipsis): 'they' must reach back over the intervening subject 'small craft' to 'the buoys laid longest', fourteen words upstream, and the elided predicate is the whole of 'sit as much as thirty-five metres from their charted places for hours together'. On first pass 'they' attaches to the nearest plural, giving the nonsense reading that small craft assume they themselves do not sit off their charted places. The wit of the clause lands, so the sentence survives, but an editor names the referent. Editor's rewrite: '...and small craft now steer to a plotted mark on the assumption that the buoys do not.'

findings.quote: Rufus Cadell has had the Marram for thirty-one years and lays his buoys long.
findings.note: class 5 (texture -- accidental numeral chime): the passage's opening measurement is 'thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water' (word 49), and Cadell's tenure is 'thirty-one years' (word 497), each preceded by 'for'. Different units and 448 words apart, so most readers will not consciously connect them, but a reader who does will hunt for a significance the piece never claims. A copy editor circles the second and moves it a year or two. Not a prosody fault in itself and not a non-native tell; pure house-style taste, hence minor. Editor's rewrite: 'Rufus Cadell has had the Marram for twenty-nine years and lays his buoys long.' CHECKED AND CLEARED in the same sweep: 'thirty-one years' (w497) to 'thirty-five metres' (w616) is 119 words with a full quotation between them, different units, both load-bearing; the ear does not hear repetition and the spelled-out form is now uniform with 'thirty-one metres', 'two hundred and fourteen', 'forty minutes', 'eleven fresh links'. findings.quote: It builds up where the chain drags on the bottom and close to the swivel.
findings.note: class 2/3 (option text -- unpunctuated coordination of unlike adjuncts): 'where the chain drags on the bottom' is a clause and 'close to the swivel' is a prepositional phrase, coordinated bare. The first reading pulls 'and close to the swivel' inside the where-clause, i.e. the chain drags both on the bottom and close to the swivel, which is a different (and on the passage's mechanism, wrong) claim. A comma resolves it. Minor, since the intended reading is the only sensible one, but this is the keyed option and an editor punctuates it. Editor's rewrite: 'It builds up where the chain drags on the bottom, and close to the swivel.'

justification: The passage states directly that wear 'gathers in the length that sweeps the ground and in the two or three links either side of the swivel', which is exactly B. A is contradicted by the opening of that same sentence, 'Wear is not spread evenly along the chain either', and by 'a chain condemned for losing a fifth of its diameter is usually condemned on a single bad metre' — the fifth-of-diameter loss is a local condemnation threshold, not a state every link reaches in three years. C introduces salt corrosion, which the text never mentions at all, and D borrows 'where the water is narrow' from the later Cadell concession about inshore aids, where it describes his change of position on scope, not any distribution of wear.

The scope paragraph explains that 'wind and tide swing the buoy about its sinker, and the more chain it has, the wider the ground it can wander over, so the light is somewhere inside that circle rather than on the cross printed on the chart', so an off-chart buoy is presumptively riding its normal swinging circle rather than having shifted its sinker — C. B reverses the stated relation (more chain, not less, means a wider circle). A over-reads the single instance of 'thirty-one metres of it for eleven metres of water' into a rule, when the whole article turns on the fact that masters choose different scopes and Cadell 'lays his buoys long'. D is unsupported: the only lifting schedule given is that the district 'lifts each of them once every three years', with no provision for an early lift on account of wander.

The lightship paragraph exists to make the point that positional uncertainty is old news: her logs 'carry, watch after watch, three bearings taken on the shore marks, because a moored ship does not sit still either and her keepers knew it', capped by Fewtrell's 'We knew the shoal was under us... Where we were over it was another question' — uncertainty long predating Prigent, who has only been 'fitting position loggers inside the hulls since 2019'. That same 'does not sit still either' kills B, which claims the vessel held station better than a buoy. C seizes on the one clause about the harbour board setting 'the cost of her crew against a lamp on a hull that needed none', but that explains one withdrawal in 1968, not a coast-wide end of manned stations 'after the war', and it is not what the paragraph is built around. D invents a comparison of vigilance with today's crews that the text never makes.

The text ends the dispute paragraph with 'Cadell has read the recordings and concedes the inshore aids, where the water is narrow. On the outer stations he has not moved' — precisely D. That sentence also refutes A, since a partial concession with the outer stations held is not giving the practice up. B attributes a cost argument to him that he never makes; his stated ground is survival — 'a buoy moored short takes the sea in its chain rather than in the water, and it is the chain that fails' — with no comparison of replacement prices anywhere in the piece. C misuses the storm, which is offered only as evidence 'too thin a series to show whether a long mooring saves buoys or has merely been lucky', and cannot be the origin of a practice held by a master who 'has had the Marram for thirty-one years'.

The piece runs the buoy 43 lift and the mechanics of scope — 'A floating aid is fixed to nothing; it is moored, and a mooring has to be slack' — straight into the Cadell/Prigent disagreement about how much slack, which it explicitly leaves open: 'Neither record disposes of the other... Prigent would like another ten years of loggers. Cadell would like a February.' That is B. A takes the single lightship paragraph for the whole. C makes the writer an advocate for loggers, but the wish for more of them is reported as Prigent's, and the closing line has buoy 43 going back 'on the scope its master chose'. D is built from one clause about the harbour board's crew costs; nothing in the text tracks a rising cost of maintaining marks.

The passage states the outcome explicitly: "Om en glipa fick sitta kvar obemärkt drog luften in, och det som skulle ha blivit kol brann i stället upp; ett par timmar räckte för att göra en hel veckas arbete till aska." B restates exactly that chain (air in, wood burns instead of charring, the charring is lost). A contradicts it by having the mila cool and the wood remain half-charred; C invents a prolonged process beyond "sex till nio dygn" that the text never claims; D is an absolutization ("ofelbart", "oavsett hur snabbt") contradicted by the conditional "fick sitta kvar obemärkt" and by the point of the round-the-clock watch.

The stated mechanism is fragility versus durability in transport: "Träkol är sprött. Varje omlastning och varje mil på ojämna vägar bröt ner bitarna till finkol och damm", while "Tjäran låg stilla i sina tunnor och kunde fraktas nedför älven, lastas om och lagras över en vinter utan att förlora i värde", and "Den skillnaden avgjorde var hantverken kunde bedrivas." D matches this. A is the exact reversal of which product was fragile; B substitutes bulk and value per barrel, which the passage never gives as the reason; C claims the resinous pine grew only far from the hyttor, which is not addressed.

Nyfeldt's objection is that the boundary may be a property line: "Vresfallets bruk ägde eller disponerade skog i en ring kring hyttan, och utanför den ringen hade bruket varken avverkningsrätt eller skäl att köpa. Det Bostrand tar för en transportgräns skulle då vara en ägogräns". A states precisely this. B inverts the causation (the bruk buying forest out to the sledge limit); C is a blanket epistemic claim she never makes; D concerns the 1870s foreman writing only surnames, which is Bostrand's own note on uneven material, not Nyfeldt's objection.

The passage supplies the seasonal complementarity that makes the combination workable: "Årstiderna skilde dem åt. Tjärdalarna brändes helst på försommaren ... medan kolmilorna restes från sensommaren och in i oktober", alongside "av dem som sålde kol till Vresfallet levererade ungefär en tredjedel också tjära något år." C follows. A is contradicted by "Tjärbränningen krävde annat virke och annat kunnande" and by the split between vakthållning and klyvning/resning; B overstates "ungefär en tredjedel" into nearly every household; D invents coercion via the kärl fee, which appears only in the pay arithmetic.

findings.quote: the buoys laid longest sit as much as thirty-five metres from their charted places for hours together
findings.note: numeral style / source-plausibility: the ruling edit puts the passage's numeric register above the corpus's observed mid-sentence spell-out ceiling. Across all 140 authentic ELF passages the largest spelled-out cardinal in the article's own voice is 'twenty degrees above normal' (host-2017-verb2-ELF-040); every measured quantity above that is in digits -- '142 feet' and '27 feet' in exemplar host-2021-verb2-ELF-040, '30 centimetres' (host-2021-verb1-ELF-037), '250 kilometres' (var-2025-verb1-ELF-032), '13,491 tonnes' (host-2015-verb1-ELF-032), 'roughly 400 residents' (var-2022-2-verb1-ELF-039). The only corpus spell-out above twenty is 'the thirty-fifth year of the reign' inside a quoted medieval charter (host-2025-verb1-ELF-037), i.e. quoted archaic register, not house style. The same charge already applied pre-repair to 'two hundred and fourteen floating aids', so the edit raises the density of an existing house-style choice rather than introducing a new one. NOT chargeable above minor: the corpus's own mastheads are digit-heavy news/science monthlies (New Scientist, The Economist, History Today, National Geographic History) and the candidate declares a BrE literary quarterly, a real style family that spells out under a hundred; and the corpus is itself not internally uniform -- host-2021-verb2-ELF-040 runs 'Twenty-seven B.C.' beside '27 feet' and digit years '80' / '117' in one excerpt. The post-repair state is at least rule-governed (every measured quantity spelled out; the surviving digits are a label, 43, and years 1911 / 1968 / 2019), where the pre-repair state rendered two same-unit measurements, 'thirty-one metres' and '35 metres', two different ways with no rule behind the split. On this dimension the edit moves toward masthead plausibility, not away.

findings.quote: What is this text mainly about?
findings.note: question style: bare deixis in the main-idea stem is off-corpus. Zero of 200 authentic ELF long-passage prompts contain 'this text'; all 24 authentic main-idea / whole-text prompts name the writer, the article or the paragraph -- 'What is the writer's main point in connection with New Orleans and Hurricane Katrina?' (var-2016-verb1-ELF-037), 'How can the basic content and tone of the article best be described?' (host-2023-verb1-ELF-037), 'What overall conclusion concerning the NHS is drawn in the text?' (var-2022-1-verb1-ELF-037). Bareness itself is fine in the corpus ('Why is Leo Tolstoy mentioned?', host-ver1-2019-verb2-ELF-038), so this is a phrasing lean toward school-comprehension register rather than a wrong question type. Untouched by the ruling repair; recorded, not charged.

findings.quote: The less chain it has been given, the further from its charted cross it is likely to lie.
findings.note: option shape/length norms: the candidate's options run long against the exemplar range. Authentic ELF long-passage prose options (n=756, cloze blocks excluded) sit at median 12 words, p75=13, p90=14, p95=16; the candidate's 20 options average 14.9 with median 15, i.e. its median option sits at the corpus p95, and 15 of 20 options are at or above the corpus p90. Max 18 is still inside the authentic range (max 31, e.g. var-2016-verb1-ELF-034 B). Verbatim-lift register is clean and is the dimension the gate names explicitly: longest common word-run with the passage is median 2 / max 5 for the candidate against median 2 / max 6 for the 800 authentic options, so options are in paraphrase register throughout. Property is program-wide and pre-existing; the ruling edit at Q1/D moved that option 14 -> 13 words, toward the corpus median.

comparative_note: Read the three exemplars end to end before the candidate. GENRE / SOURCE-PLAUSIBILITY: pass. 'Buoy 43, Off Cleyburn' reads as first-hand working reportage with the non-thesis residue the exemplars carry -- the fog bell 'the older skippers still call the worst sound on that coast', logs that 'are mostly weather', the hull painted twice a year, 'Then the deck is hosed down' -- against var-2016-verb1-ELF-033, which likewise hangs a quoted practitioner ('This was a lousy place to put a city.') off dated particulars, and host-2023-verb1-ELF-033, which runs a named authorial voice through a working argument. No topic-sentence symmetry, no one-claim-per-paragraph tidiness: P3 is a genuine digression that does not serve the thesis. At 781 words it sits mid-range for the class (exemplars 570-823). The bare dash byline '- Fenella Moye' is off the corpus form 'Name, Publication' (host-2021-verb2-ELF-040 closes 'Luis Baena del Alcazar, National Geographic History'), but it is the established program house style across batches 3-15 and declining to invent a masthead is the conservative choice; not charged. INTELLECTUAL TEMPERATURE: pass, at or above the exemplar mean -- two practitioners with different evidence types, a real trade-off (scope buys survival and costs positional accuracy), and an ending left genuinely open ('Neither record disposes of the other'), which is a harder register than host-2021-verb2-ELF-040's settled architectural exposition. QUESTION STYLE: pass. 'What is implied about...' is the corpus's single most common stem family (23 instances); Q3's 'Why does the writer mention the lightship...' has direct precedent in 'Why is Leo Tolstoy mentioned?' (host-ver1-2019-verb2-ELF-038) and 'Why is Triumph of the Will mentioned by the reviewer?' (var-2022-2-verb2-ELF-040); Q3's all-'To' option set matches host-2021-verb1-ELF-033; the Q1/Q4 shared stem frame matches blocks that repeat 'What is said...' twice (var-2023-verb1-ELF-034/036, host-2018-verb1-ELF-034/036); all-four-options-share-a-first-word, as at Q3 and Q4, occurs in 65 of 200 authentic questions. ON THE THREE RULING EDITS SPECIFICALLY: (a) 'where the channel is narrow' is register-improving -- 13 words at the corpus p75, longest common run with the passage of 2 tokens (the corpus median), so the tightened lure does not become a verbatim string; (b) 'a re-lay' has an exact corpus analogue inside the pool exemplar itself, host-2021-verb2-ELF-040's 'a literal re-creation of the cosmos' -- the same disambiguating re- hyphen, and one of only two such forms in the whole ELF corpus; (c) the thirty-one / thirty-one / thirty-five prosody is not a tell: the two 'thirty-one' spans are 448 words and two paragraphs apart on different nouns (metres of chain, years of service) and 'thirty-five' falls 119 words after 'thirty-one years' across a quotation and a new speaker's introduction, and the pool exemplar recycles a numeral the same way, using 27 for two unrelated quantities ('Twenty-seven B.C.' and 'about 27 feet across'). Verdict pass: the unit would sit unremarked next to the three exemplars, and none of the three ruling edits moved it toward the edge.

findings.quote: medan tjäran tog liten plats och gav ett högt värde per tunna
findings.note: class 6 (idiomatisk temperatur), q2 option B: 'ge ett värde' is the measurement collocation in Swedish ('mätningen gav ett högt värde'), not the commercial one, so for goods it reads a half-step off. A native sub would write 'hade ett högt värde per tunna' or, in trade prose, 'betingade ett högt pris per tunna'. Grammatical and understandable, hence minor and not major; native alternative: 'medan tjäran tog liten plats och hade ett högt värde per tunna'.

findings.quote: Varje sådan glipa förstör ofelbart hela lasten, oavsett hur snabbt kolaren hinner ingripa.
findings.note: class 6 (idiomatisk temperatur), q1 option D: 'lasten' is used in this passage for charcoal already in transit ('en last med mycket finmaterial', 'slädlast'); the wood standing inside a mila is not normally 'en last'. The kolning register would say 'hela milan' or 'hela kolningen'. 'ofelbart' as an adverb ('utan undantag') is fine and stays. Native alternative: 'Varje sådan glipa förstör ofelbart hela milan, oavsett hur snabbt kolaren hinner ingripa.'

findings.quote: Vad kan man, utifrån texten, dra för slutsats av att samma hushåll kunde bedriva båda hantverken?
findings.note: class 5/6 (register + temperatur), q4 stem: the split 'vad ... för slutsats' is neutral-to-spoken Swedish, and wedging the parenthetical 'utifrån texten' between 'man' and 'dra' pulls the two halves of the construction further apart, so the stem reads clunkier than the other three ('Vad händer, enligt texten, om ...' is clean because nothing is split). Edited exam prose would use the unsplit form. Native alternative: 'Vilken slutsats kan man dra av att samma hushåll kunde bedriva båda hantverken?'

findings.quote: medan tjäran tog liten plats och gav ett högt värde per tunna
findings.note: class 6 (kollokation), q2 option B: 'gav ett högt värde' evokes a measured value rather than commercial worth; 'hade ett högt värde per tunna' / 'betingade ett högt pris per tunna' is what a native trade-prose writer produces. Taste-level, grammatical, no reader will be misled.

findings.quote: Eftersom tjäran var ömtålig fick den bara framställas nära vattenvägar
findings.note: class 2 (interpunktion, taste-level), q2 option A: Svenska skrivregler recommends a comma between a fronted subordinate clause and the following main clause; the same omission occurs in the passage ('Om en glipa fick sitta kvar obemärkt drog luften in'). Widely omitted in published Swedish, so minor, not a conviction of the text's nativeness. Native alternative: 'Eftersom tjäran var ömtålig, fick den bara framställas nära vattenvägar'.

findings.quote: gav ett högt värde per tunna
findings.note: class 6 (kollokation), q2 option B: 'ge ett värde' is the measurement idiom; for a commodity a native writes 'hade ett högt värde per tunna' or 'betingade ett högt pris per tunna'. Only conviction the category sweep produced in the option set.
